messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up re: credential sharding + route contracts. thinking about tightening API key surface to reduce blast radius and simplify runtime decisioning. want opinions on tradeoffs before we lock the migration plan.
ryan: quick context pls — what's the main pain?
tess: incidents + audit showed long-lived org keys used by 3rd-party jobs, and one leaked key touched many projects. also runtime does a lot of global lookups to resolve route entitlements — perf + cache churn.
maria: exact. two goals: 1) reduce lateral access from leaked keys, 2) make authz checks cache-friendly and predictable.
jonathan: naive question — why not just TTL every key and call it a day?
maria: TTL helps but breaks UX for long-running infra tasks and operators. proposal: keep long-lived org-admin keys for humans + ops, but introduce sharded project-bound keys for services, and ephemeral operator tokens for cross-project jobs.
tess: important callout: we need a clear runtime contract per route: either route accepts org-key OR requires project-scoped key. that lets us avoid full-graph entitlement checks for common paths.
ryan: that route contract idea seems powerful. can we express it as simple metadata? eg: in route config: auth_mode: [org,project,operator] or auth_mode: project_only
maria: exactly. example: 
```
POST /v1/models/generate:
  auth_mode: [project]   # requires project-scoped key or delegation token
GET /v1/usage:
  auth_mode: [org,project] # dashboards allowed with org keys
```
jonathan: runtime implication: if route is project_only we can key cache by project id and avoid expensive cross-lookup. big perf win.
tess: migration headaches: many customers and internal services currently use org-scoped keys in code. what's the plan to migrate without breaking jobs?
maria: proposed phased plan: 
- phase 1: implement route contract + runtime enforcement (soft log + metric on violations)
- phase 2: issue tooling to mint project-bound keys and a dev-friendly shim that exchanges org->project token for local testing
- phase 3: opt-in enforcement for internal infra routes (enforce project_only)
- phase 4: public enforcement after 90 days and mailing cadence
ryan: +1. add a fallback policy: if project token missing and org key present, allow a 1-minute exchange flow for long-running jobs to mint a scoped delegation token — log & rate-limit heavily.
jonathan: re: operator tokens: do we require HSM/KMS-backed signing for those? ops teams will want rotation guarantees.
tess: we should require KMS for any token that can impersonate other projects (operator). project-scoped keys can be standard API keys with shorter TTLs and scoped claims.
maria: revocation model: publish per-key revocation-vector and maintain a short-lived cache in runtime. target max revocation latency 30s for operator tokens, 5min for project keys, 24h for legacy org keys (during transition).
ryan: revocation latency matters for compromise. are we confident caches can evict quickly across regions?
jonathan: add central invalidation bus (pub/sub) + local best-effort cache flush. where bus unavailable, fall back to TTL enforcement.
tess: telemetry/metrics to track: token-usage by scope, violation-rate per route, avg authz lookup latency, cache hit rate by project, cross-project access incidents.
maria: yes. also add an automated alert when a single key appears to access >N distinct projects in 24h (N configurable) — likely leak.
ryan: how do we store project binding in keys? embed the project id in token claims (signed) vs keep mapping in DB?
maria: prefer embedded claim for fast routing (signed JWT-like claim or MACed header). keep DB mapping for human keys and allow lookup when claim absent.
jonathan: security note: signed claim means we must handle key rotation gracefully. include key id (kid) and support multi-kid verification during rotation windows.
tess: UX note for SDKs: provide a local exchange client `redwood key exchange --project X` that mints scoped token for dev & CI. keep org-key->exchange gated by admin permission.
maria: migration checklist for internal services (summary): 
1) add route contract metadata to service configs
2) update SDKs to prefer project-scoped keys and provide exchange shim
3) enable soft enforcement & observe logs/metrics 2 weeks
4) opt-in enforcement for internal infra 2 weeks after that
5) open public timeline and enable enforcement after 90 days
jonathan: + add a canary group of services that flip to strict now to validate perf & support churn.
ryan: one more: introspection endpoint for tokens (who/what scope) — rate-limited and allowed only for ops/sec roles. needed for debugging.
tess: agree. protect it heavily and log every lookup.
maria: any objections? otherwise I'll draft a short RFC and the migration playbook + telemetry dashboard template.
ryan: no objections. looks solid. curious about perf numbers after canary.
jonathan: +1. please include exact cache eviction TTLs in RFC and the exchange flow pseudo-code.
maria: will do. ping me if you want to be in the canary cohort.
ops-bot: scheduled: feature-flag rollout for route_contracts begins 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC (:calendar:).
